lessons.title: Lesson 1: Welcome and What You’re Building
lessons.goal: You understand what this course is, what you will be able to do by Friday, and have your MacBook workspace folder ready before touching any tools.
sections: What is this course?

This is a 4 week hands on internship where you learn to use AI tools the way a real business uses them. By the end you will have built a working AI workspace, created real content, completed live business projects, and packaged everything into a portfolio you can show employers. You are not expected to know any of this yet. That is the whole point.
What you will learn this week

Week 1 is about getting your tools set up and working. By Friday you will have access to Claude (an AI thinking partner), Codex (an AI building partner), and a Telegram agent (a chat window where you can talk to an AI assistant). You will also learn how to save your work so you can pick up right where you left off.
Meet the tools

Claude is like a smart coworker who helps you write, plan, and think through problems. Codex is a tool that helps you build, review, and check work. Telegram is a messaging app where you will talk to an AI agent that CJ set up. Google Drive is where you back up your files so nothing gets lost. You will set up each one in the next few lessons, one at a time.
MacBook ready check
Charge the MacBook, connect to WiFi, and update Chrome. Clean out the Downloads folder so new files are easy to find. Bookmark this course page in Chrome so you can get back here fast.
Create the AI Workspace folder

Open Finder on the MacBook. Go to Documents and create a new folder called AI Workspace. Inside it, create three folders: Proof, Notes, and Exports. This is where all your work lives for the next four weeks.
Cloud first rule

We do not know how much memory this MacBook has, so we use browser tools instead of installing heavy software. Everything in this course runs in Chrome or Safari. If a video shows someone typing commands in a black window (called a terminal), just watch it as a demo. Do not install anything on the MacBook unless CJ says to do it while sitting next to you.
Submit

Take a screenshot of your AI Workspace folder in Finder showing the three subfolders. Write one sentence about what you think this course will teach you. That is it for Lesson 1. The real setup starts in Lesson 2.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Set Up Hermes and Your Telegram Agent
lessons.goal: You install Hermes on your Mac, connect it to Codex for AI power, create a Telegram bot, and prove you can message your own agent from your phone.
sections: What are we building?

Hermes is an AI agent that runs on your Mac. Telegram is the messaging app you will use to talk to it from your phone. By the end of this lesson you will have your own AI agent you can message any time.
Step 1: Install Hermes

Open the Terminal app on your Mac (search for Terminal in Spotlight). Paste this one line and press enter: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/main/scripts/install.sh | bash. Wait for it to finish. That is the only time you need to type in Terminal today.
Step 2: Run the setup wizard
In the same Terminal window, type: hermes setup. Choose quick setup when it asks. When it asks for a provider, pick OpenAI Codex.
Step 3: Connect your Codex account

Hermes will show you a link. Click it to open your browser. Sign into your ChatGPT account. It will show you a 9 digit code. Copy that code, go back to Terminal, paste it in, and press enter. That connects Hermes to the AI brain.
Step 4: Install Telegram and create your bot

Download Telegram on your phone from the App Store or Google Play. Open Telegram and search for @BotFather. Send /newbot and follow the prompts to name your bot. BotFather will reply with a bot token (a long string of letters and numbers). Copy that token. Never share bot tokens in public docs or screenshots.
Step 5: Get your Telegram user ID
In Telegram, search for @userinfobot and send it any message. It will reply with your user ID (a number like 123456789). Write that number down.
Step 6: Connect Telegram to Hermes

Back in Terminal, type: hermes gateway setup. When it asks which platform, pick Telegram. Paste your bot token and your user ID when prompted. Then type: hermes gateway start. Your bot should come online within seconds.
Step 7: Test and prove it

Open your bot chat in Telegram and send a test message. Wait for Hermes to respond. Screenshot the conversation. Write down the bot name and how to reopen the chat tomorrow. Add everything to your proof log.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: What Did You Just Build? The Language of AI Tools

video.title: What are AI agents? AI Agents Explained in 2 minutes
video.purpose: Quick visual intro to agents before CJ examples.

lessons.goal: You can explain the core agent language in plain English and connect each word to the setup you just built.
sections: Start from what you built

Look at your setup proof. Claude is a cloud LLM. Codex is a build focused AI tool. Telegram is a front door. Hermes is the agent system behind that front door. The MacBook is just the workstation, not the brain.
LLM vs agent
An LLM thinks and answers. An agent thinks and acts with tools, memory, rules, and a goal. Simple line: chatbot answers, agent gets work done.
Cloud vs local
A cloud model runs on someone else's servers through the browser or app. A local model runs on the laptop and needs more RAM and setup. For this course, use cloud models unless CJ says otherwise.
Watch with purpose
Watch the 2 minute agent clip. Write down the first moment where the video moves from talking to doing.
Building blocks
A command tells the agent what to do. A skill is a saved best practice. A tool lets the agent touch the outside world. An MCP is a clean way to connect tools and data.
Build
Add a glossary to my-ai-workspace.md with: LLM, agent, command, skill, tool, MCP, wiki, vault, closeout, Drive backup. Use your own words.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Markdown, Saved Work, Drive Backup, and Closeout

video.title: Learn The Basics Of Markdown in 10 Minutes
video.purpose: Shows Markdown as simple structured text before you build workspace files.

lessons.goal: You build the habit of saving useful work in Markdown, backing it up, and closing the loop with proof.
sections: Markdown is the playbook
Markdown is plain text with structure. Use headings, bullets, links, screenshots, and checklists. It keeps work readable for people and useful for agents.
Set up your workspace the right way
Start every workspace with clear context, examples, constraints, and proof. The AI should not have to guess where things live or what good looks like.
Drive backup
Local files are not enough. On the MacBook, keep the working folder in Documents, then back up the AI Workspace folder to Google Drive so Rea can recover progress and CJ can review proof.
Mac folder habit
Use Finder the same way every time: Documents > AI Workspace for work, Downloads for temporary files, and Google Drive for backup. If a file lands in Downloads, move it before closing the laptop.
Closeout habit
Every session ends with what changed, where it lives, proof, and the next step. If it is not written down, it did not happen.
Build
Create or update my-ai-workspace.md, prompts.md, proof-log.md, and closeout.md. Add today’s Mac setup notes, cloud tool links, and one clean next step.

lessons.goal: You finish with a real AI workspace, saved progress, a Drive backup, and a clear resume point.
sections: Project brief

Build My AI Workspace for a MacBook cloud setup. It should prove you can log into Claude, use Codex or OpenAI, message the Telegram agent, explain the agent language, save Markdown files, and back everything up to Drive.
Before you leave tomorrow
You should be able to close the MacBook, reopen it, open Documents > AI Workspace, open the course bookmark, open the Drive backup, and message the Telegram agent without CJ hunting for files.
Progress save
Use the Save progress button in this course. Download the progress file. Upload it to the AI Workspace folder in Google Drive.
Drive backup
Back up my-ai-workspace.md, prompts.md, proof-log.md, closeout.md, the glossary, and screenshots to Drive. The rule is simple: local work plus cloud proof.
Closeout
Write one closeout note: what was set up, what worked, what is still missing, where the files live, and what the next step is.
Submit
Submit the Drive folder link or screenshot, the downloaded progress file, the final closeout note, and one MacBook resume checklist showing exactly how to start again tomorrow.
